key_themes: Q3 earnings season peak driving large stock-specific moves
Salesforce acquires Braze for $5.66B — marquee M&A deal of the day
Value/cyclical rotation as tech names show mixed guidance; SMCI and SpaceX strong but Netflix disappoints

stocks.discussion_driver: Salesforce announced a definitive agreement to acquire Braze for $47.50/share in all-cash (~$5.66B total), sending BRZE up 51.7% to $45.57 after trading was halted premarket. The deal is expected to close in Salesforce’s fiscal 2028 pending shareholder and regulatory approval, with Braze’s board unanimously backing the offer.
bull_case: Acquisition price of $47.50 offers ~4.2% upside from current $45.57 with high deal certainty — all-cash offer, unanimous board approval, $5.66B enterprise value
Salesforce’s massive enterprise CRM install base creates significant cross-sell opportunity for Braze’s customer engagement platform post-close
bear_case: Deal closes in fiscal 2028, tying up capital for 12+ months with only a ~4% spread to acquisition price and meaningful regulatory/execution risk
If the deal falls through under antitrust scrutiny, the stock would likely revert toward pre-announcement levels (~$30), representing ~34% downside
stocks.vs_52wk_high: +0.1% above prior 52-week high ($45.54); new 52-week high set today
stocks.analyst_rating: Hold (post-deal consensus; Stifel raised target to $47.50 and downgraded to Hold)

stocks.discussion_driver: Equifax beat Q3 2026 estimates with adj. EPS of $2.26 vs. $2.20 consensus; revenue of $1.69B came in line. Shares jumped ~10-12% to ~$175 as the beat offset management trimming full-year revenue guidance due to persistent U.S. mortgage market weakness. The company also announced a $750M acquisition of Circúlo de Crédito, expanding into Latin America.
bull_case: Consecutive EPS beats demonstrate core data analytics business resilience even as the mortgage market headwind persists into 2027
$750M Circúlo de Crédito acquisition diversifies revenue into the high-growth Latin American credit bureau market, reducing U.S. mortgage dependence
bear_case: Full-year revenue guidance trimmed again due to U.S. mortgage weakness; forward EPS guidance midpoint of $8.50 reflects an ongoing structural headwind
Multiple analyst price target cuts (Morgan Stanley to $205, RBC to $177, Oppenheimer downgraded to Perform) signal limited near-term Street confidence

stocks.discussion_driver: Myriad Genetics announced a definitive agreement to sell its Prenatal Health testing business to Labcorp for $210M cash (plus inventory value at closing), with the deal expected to close by early 2027. The transaction provides significant cash relative to Myriad’s ~$600M market cap and lets management focus on hereditary cancer testing and pharmacogenomics, driving shares up ~37% to ~$5.54.
bull_case: $210M Labcorp deal provides substantial cash inflow relative to Myriad’s ~$600M market cap, enabling meaningful debt reduction and strategic refocusing
Shedding the prenatal unit lets Myriad concentrate on hereditary cancer testing and pharmacogenomics, where it holds stronger competitive positioning and IP
bear_case: Company remains unprofitable with negative EPS; pre-deal consensus was ‘Reduce’ and core business path to profitability is still unproven
Labcorp deal removes ~$160M in annual revenue from Myriad’s top line, significantly shrinking the company’s scale going forward
stocks.analyst_rating: Hold/Reduce (mixed; Piper Sandler upgraded to Neutral/$5, TD Cowen Hold/$4.50, Craig-Hallum $8)

stocks.discussion_driver: Super Micro raised fiscal Q1 2027 revenue guidance to $18.5–19.5B from prior $14.5–15.5B, a ~$4B increase driven by surging AI server demand. Gross margin outlook also improved to 12.0–12.5% vs. prior 10.4–10.8%. The stock closed at $32.47 in regular trading and then surged 11–13% in after-hours on the guidance raise.
bull_case: Massive ~$4B revenue guidance raise confirms SMCI as a primary beneficiary of the ongoing enterprise AI infrastructure buildout cycle with accelerating demand
Improving gross margin outlook (12.0–12.5% vs. prior 10.4–10.8%) signals meaningful operating leverage materializing as AI server volumes scale
bear_case: Stock remains -42.6% below its 52-week high of $56.60, reflecting lingering investor concern about historical accounting irregularities and governance
Intense competition from Dell and HPE in AI servers limits SMCI’s long-term pricing power and gross margin sustainability

stocks.discussion_driver: Hasbro delivered a strong Q3 2026 beat with adj. EPS of $2.90 vs. $1.86 consensus and revenue of $1.59B vs. $1.48B forecast, driven by record Magic: The Gathering sales, favorable tariff refunds, and improved margins. The company raised full-year guidance (7–9% revenue growth, EBITDA $1.575–1.625B) and doubled its buyback target, pushing shares up ~10.5% to a new 52-week high.
bull_case: Record Magic: The Gathering sales and raised full-year guidance confirm durable strength in Hasbro’s digital-physical franchise model with multiple revenue streams
Doubled share buyback target and strong cash generation signal management confidence in sustained profitability and shareholder capital return
bear_case: Stock is now near the analyst average target of $110.64, leaving limited near-term upside after the post-earnings surge to a new 52-week high
Q3 benefited from one-time tariff refunds that may not recur; ongoing tariff uncertainty and toy industry cyclicality pose risks to future quarters
